prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1499; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant reporting a low-speed head-on collision at a local intersection, with a complaint of back pain and a request to open an injury file. Claimant is unrepresented and was willing to provide a recorded statement.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. Assigned the file for vehicle damage inspection and injury review.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account of the collision that matches the claimant's description of how it happened. Requested the responding officer's report.

Entry 4: Police report received and confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. Two independent witnesses were identified and contacted; both describe the impact in terms consistent with the claimant's account.

Entry 5: Photographs from the scene and from the vehicle were received and reviewed. The visible damage is largely in line with the impact described by all parties.

Entry 6: Vehicle inspection completed. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records, and nothing points to any damage predating the start of coverage.

Entry 7: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Account of the collision was consistent with the first notice of loss, and the claimant has repeated the same account in every conversation since.

Entry 8: Medical records received for the initial emergency visit. Diagnosis is a back strain, which fits the kind and force of a low-speed frontal impact. No prior treatment to the same body area is known from available records.

Entry 9: Claimant attended physical therapy on a standard schedule. Treatment notes show steady improvement, and the frequency of sessions has been reduced accordingly.

Entry 10: Reviewed the injury file with the nurse reviewer, who agreed that the treatment course is typical for this type of injury and that the reported symptoms align with the mechanism of the collision.

Entry 11: Claimant reports most symptoms have resolved and is near the end of the planned course of care. Follow-up with the treating provider is scheduled to confirm discharge.

Entry 12: File reviewed and all key facts checked against the evidence gathered. Liability and injury appear consistent with the documented collision, and the file is ready for settlement evaluation.
